summits.name: Partnership Summit 2016
summits.long_name: 22nd CII Partnership Summit, branded by the state as Sunrise Andhra Pradesh
summits.quote: During Partnership Summit held in 2016, 328 MoUs with a potential investment of Rs. 4,67,577 crore and an employment potential of 9,58,896 people were signed.

summits.name: Partnership Summit 2017
summits.long_name: 23rd CII Partnership Summit, also known as the Sunrise Andhra Pradesh Investment Meet
summits.quote: 664 MoUs were signed with anticipated investment of Rs. 10.54 lakh crore and employment potential of 22.34 lakh.

summits.name: Partnership Summit 2018
summits.quote: In the recently concluded Partnership Summit 2018, the Government signed another 734 MoUs with investment potential of Rs 4.39 lakh crore and employment potential of 11 lakh.

summits.name: Global Investors Summit 2023
summits.long_name: Advantage Andhra Pradesh Global Investors Summit
summits.quote: The Global Investors' Summit held in March 2023 resulted in securing 386 agreements with investments worth Rs. 13.11 lakh crore and additional job potential of 6.07 lakh.

summits.name: Partnership Summit 2025
summits.quote: At the recently held Global Partnership Summit 2025, Andhra Pradesh secured investment commitments exceeding Rs. 13.25 lakh crore, with employment potential over 16.13 lakh, and 610 MoUs were signed.

by_year.missing_reason: Not published. We read the Budget Speech 2015-16, where a 2014-15 figure would sit, and the Budget Speech 2016-17. Neither contains the word grounded or any achievement figure for that year. The state's first grounded sentence is for 2015-16.

by_year.basis: Grounded private investment, MSME plus large and mega
by_year.quote: In total, we have grounded private investments worth Rs. 9,505 crores and created 76,818 jobs in MSMEs, large and mega Industries in 2015-16.

by_year.basis: Large and mega industrial projects only. No MSME figure for 2016-17 appears in any survey we hold, so this is not on the same basis as the years either side of it.
by_year.quote: During 2016-17, 54 Large and Mega industrial projects are established with an investment of Rs.4881.13 Crore and employment generation of 22696 persons.
by_year.source_publisher: Planning Department, Government of Andhra Pradesh, Socio Economic Survey 2017-18, Industries chapter
by_year.missing_reason: Not published as an achievement. The Budget Speech 2016-17 set a target of grounding Rs 11,500 crore in 2016-17, and the Budget Speech 2017-18, where the result would appear, reports only summit MoU potential instead. A target is not an outcome, and the only realisation number offered is a hit rate of about 48 per cent whose denominator the speech never states. We read both speeches and the Socio Economic Survey 2017-18 to be sure.

by_year.basis: Large and mega Rs 4,296.91 crore plus MSME Rs 2,382.65 crore, added here. That matches the basis of the published years, but the period does not.
by_year.quote: During 2017-18 (upto Dec 2017), 40 Large and Mega industrial projects are established with an investment of Rs.4296.91 Crore ... During 2017-18 (upto Dec 2017) 5920 Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises were established, providing employment to 59,103 with an investment of Rs.2382.65 Crores.
by_year.source_publisher: Planning Department, Government of Andhra Pradesh, Socio Economic Survey 2017-18, Industries chapter
by_year.missing_reason: No annual figure published. The Budget Speech 2018-19 gives 26,368 MSME units with Rs 11,779 crore, but attaches no period to it, and against the 10,068 units the state reported for 2018-19 alone it is plainly a running total since bifurcation rather than one year. Its large and mega figure is a tracked pipeline, not construction. We will not present a cumulative stock as an annual flow.

definition.title: Read the grounded column carefully
definition.body: Andhra Pradesh has never published a clean, consistent series of how much announced investment actually got built. Across eleven budget speeches and surveys the state uses at least three different ideas, and calls them all the same thing: 'grounded private investments' (2015-16), 'projects commenced operations with committed investment' (2017-18, where the rupee figure is the money the company promised, not the money it spent), 'units established with an investment of' (2018-19 onwards), and 'commenced production' plus 'MSME established' as separate components (the Socio Economic Surveys for 2022-23 and 2023-24). The reporting periods do not line up either: some are financial years, one is June to April, one stops at 31 December. Five of the twelve years since bifurcation have no published grounded figure at all. We show what exists, mark what is missing, and do not interpolate. Nobody should read this as a like-for-like scoreboard, because the state never published one.
definition.sources_note: The gaps are not our omission. They are what the state chose not to publish.
